findings.title: Data race on shared err variable across errgroup goroutines in init
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each goroutine launched via group.Go executes `_, _, err = s.build(...)`, assigning to the `err` variable declared in the outer function scope. With s.initWorkers > 1, multiple goroutines write to this shared variable concurrently while group.Wait() and the surrounding code read it, which is a data race (Go race detector will flag it). Each goroutine should use its own local error variable and return it: `_, _, berr := s.build(...); return berr`.

findings.title: Unsynchronized increment of totalBatchesIndexed from concurrent goroutines
findings.body: totalBatchesIndexed is incremented inside the errgroup goroutines (`totalBatchesIndexed++`) without any synchronization. With multiple init workers this is a concurrent read/write race and the final count reported in the tracing span event can be wrong. Use an atomic counter or increment outside the goroutines (e.g., from len(stats)).

findings.title: Removing the whole-function lock allows concurrent BuildIndex for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its entire duration, which serialized index builds. Now the lock is only taken when inserting into the cache, so two concurrent callers can build an index for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously (e.g., getOrCreateIndex racing between a Search request and a watch event after init, since getOrCreateIndex has no per-key locking). For file-backed indexes both builds call bleve.New on the same directory, and the second one will fail because bleve locks the index directory; the loser also discards its work and one build silently overwrites the other in the cache. A per-key lock (singleflight) is needed to keep the speedup without allowing duplicate builds of the same key.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu (RLock). Now that BuildIndex writes to b.cache concurrently (during parallel init and from watch-event-driven getOrCreateIndex builds), TotalDocs can run concurrently with a map write — init itself calls s.search.TotalDocs() while other builds may still be triggered by handleEvent. Concurrent map read/write is a fatal error in Go ("concurrent map read and map write"). Take b.cacheMu.RLock() around the iteration.

findings.title: NewResourceServer leaks the cancelable context and partially started watchers on Init failure
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and returns an error if it fails, but on that error path s.cancel() is never called. If search.init succeeded but initWatcher failed (or vice versa partially), the background watch goroutine(s) and poller started during init keep running with no way to stop them, since the constructor returned nil and the caller has no server handle to Stop. Call s.cancel() (and ideally s.Stop) before returning the error.
